newsitem.title: UKRAINE: UKRAINE FOREIGN BOND DEBUT TO HELP WAGES CRISIS-PM.
newsitem.headline: UKRAINE FOREIGN BOND DEBUT TO HELP WAGES CRISIS-PM.

text.p: Ukraine plans to put nearly half its earnings from an international $450-million one-year note issued this week towards paying off its $3.6 billion wage debt, Prime Minister Valery Pustovoitenko said on Wednesday.
The notes, launched on Monday ahead of planned Samurai bond and dollar-dominated Eurobond debuts this year, were expected to raise $410 million.

"One of the government's main goals is to pay off our wage, pension and student stipend debt," Pustovoitenko told a news conference. "We will pay 371 million hryvnias from the bonds we issued this week toward paying wages."
The ever-growing wage debt, which stood at $2.3 billion at the end of March, is owed to government workers, pensioners and university students.
Bankers Trust Luxembourg SA issued the $450 million debut on Monday. Nomura International was the underwriter.
Pustovoitenko's first promise after being appointed late last month was to nullify wage arrears.

Ukrainian officials have said the former Soviet republic, in the process of obtaining international credit ratings, planned to issue two more international bonds this year which could raise up to $1 billion.
